messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'helix-health-prod' gpu_util at 100% and request queue growing. Tenant: HelixHealth (tenant_id=tenant-4732). Pager triggered to #incidents and #eng-oncall.

mike_oncall: ack — I'm awake, looking.

leo_sre: saw the spike, autoscaler didn't spin up new machines. API to provision extra GPUs returned quota error: "Failed to allocate: region gpu quota exceeded".

mike_oncall: cs_jordan, are customers impacted? priority? :phone:

cs_jordan: HelixHealth support called. They're seeing timeouts and elevated 429s on their production clinical-triage flows. High business impact — some clinics are in degraded mode. I'm on the call with them now.

mike_oncall: alright forming short-lived war room. @infra-dave can we burst to shared/hosted capacity as a quick mitigation?

infra-dave: technically yes, we have spare capacity in our shared cluster but HelixHealth is deployed in a Private VPC dedicated pool. Contractually they restrict cross-tenant hosting. Need legal + sales ok before we move data out of VPC.

sales-karim: I can ping legal, but for an emergency they might permit a one-time fallback if we log and isolate traffic. I'll get verbal ok and follow with written.

anya_prod: propose immediate mitigations (short-term):
1) throttle HelixHealth request concurrency & background workers.
2) downgrade non-critical models to quantized variants to cut GPU time.
3) manual burst: allocate 4x GPUs from spare capacity (manual provisioning).

eng-kate: I can push the throttle rule now and roll out model-variant flags for lower priority routes.

(ops log snippet):
```
pool: helix-health-prod
gpu_total: 8
gpu_used: 8
queued_requests: 842
avg_latency_ms: 1400
error_5xx_rate: 12%
```

mike_oncall: ok do step 1 now. Update tenant policy: concurrency=4 and rate_limit=200rps. eng-kate, deploy?

eng-kate: applying throttling policy now... patch deployed to config service. Starting to shed low-priority traffic.

mike_oncall: monitoring — any immediate wins?

eng-kate: queues down to ~320 after 6 minutes, avg latency ~700ms, 5xx down to ~4%. Reduced noise but still elevated.

mike_oncall: good. infra-dave, please request manual GPU allocation as contingency. If queued_requests >500 again within 30m, we trigger manual burst.

infra-dave: requested manual allocation of 4x GPUs from spare cluster. Ops lead approval required — pinged @ops-lead. ETA once approved ~8 minutes to be ready.

ops-lead: approved emergency allocation under incident code SC-EMG-2195. Allocating now.

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 2h — next primary: leo_sre.

mike_oncall: handoff notes for whoever picks this up: throttled tenant concurrency to 4, CS informed, sales is pursuing legal for hosted fallback, manual GPUs requested and being provisioned, watching queues and latencies. Keep monitoring for 1h then evaluate rollback.

cs_jordan: I'll update HelixHealth support channel: telling them we've applied throttling and are provisioning additional GPUs. Setting customer expectation: degraded throughput for next 30-60 mins while we stabilize.

sales-karim: legal gave verbal emergency approval referencing contract clause SC-61. If required we can fail traffic to a hosted burst with strict logging and revocable access. Documenting and following up formally.

mike_oncall: creating follow-up ticket INCIDENT-2195-helix-gpu-exhaustion for postmortem / capacity plan. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml for root cause (autoscaling and quota behaviour).

mike_oncall: handing ownership to @leo_sre for next hour. Leo — please own next updates and finalize mitigation decisions.

leo_sre: on it. taking ownership. I'll post updates every 15m and coordinate with infra/eng. (react:eyes)

mike_oncall: thanks team. leaving war room — ping me if manual burst is needed or customer impact worsens.

(ends)
